sources.use: Highest-confidence model-specific source in this set for an actual conventional sensitive altimeter's part organization and mechanism layout. Envelope dimensions remain unknown.
locator: PDF p.11, printed p.2-4, Figure 2-1: exploded outer case, bezel/window, dial/pointers, pressure case, adjustment and mounting pieces; numbered callouts link to the repair-parts list.

PDF p.12, printed p.2-5, Figure 2-2: exploded mechanism assembly, including plates, aneroid/diaphragm-linked pieces, shafts, gears, springs, jewel/bearing parts and adjustment elements; manual disassembly instructions and parts list provide complementary naming.
PDF p.7, printed p.1-2, Table 1-1: 35,000-ft indication range and 28.1-31.0 inHg barometric setting range. These are operating ranges, not physical dimensions.

PDF pp.15-17 contain further mechanism assembly, calibration and adjustment detail. The manual states 0.003-inch end-play settings for mechanism wheels/shafts and a 0.005-inch-thick shim; these are assembly/fit values, not an overall envelope or complete component dimension set. It also specifies a standard 1/8-inch IPT static fitting in the leak-test procedure.

sources.title: Customer Acceptance Specification, Indicator-Altimeter, United Instruments Spec. No. UI5934, drawing/document d116799
sources.use: Strong exterior-envelope source for an actual United UI5934 altimeter; pair only as an explicitly cross-manufacturer envelope reference if modeling Kollsman internals.
locator: PDF p.1, drawing: dimensioned front and side views, pointer/barometric configurations, and port locations. The case is specified per MS33549 and the port 1/8-27 ANPT per MIL-P-7105.
PDF p.1 explicitly dimensions 3.248 in typical across the case/front view and 4.0 in maximum case depth. These are stated OEM drawing dimensions, not measurements inferred from pixels.
PDF pp.2-8 include pressure-altitude/pressure-difference and test/acceptance information, not internal exploded mechanism parts.

sources.title: Indicator-Rate of Climb, United Instruments Spec. No. UI7000 (revision F)
sources.use: Best OEM exterior-envelope and performance source found for an actual conventional United mechanical VSI/rate-of-climb family; pair with Army Figure 4-12 only as generic internal architecture, not as the UI7000's confirmed internals.
locator: PDF p.4, OEM drawing: dimensioned face and side views for UI7000-series configurations, with case per MS33549 and 1/8-27 ANPT ports per MIL-P-7105.
PDF p.1 describes pressure-difference operation, single pointer, range and zero setting; PDF pp.2-3 provide performance/tolerance criteria.

sources.title: Indicator-Airspeed, United Instruments Spec. No. UI8000 (revision E)
sources.use: Best OEM exterior-envelope and operating-range source found for an actual United mechanical ASI; pair with Army Figure 4-11 only as generic internal architecture, not as the UI8000's confirmed internals.
locator: PDF p.1 states the airspeed operating principle: differential between pitot and static pressure produces the pointer indication; calibrated range for part 8000 is 0-200 mph, 8025 is 0-250 mph, and 8030 is 0-300 mph.
PDF p.7, OEM drawing: dimensioned front/side views, case per MS33549, and pitot/static port thread 1/8-27 ANPT per MIL-P-7105.

sources.title: Aviation Unit Maintenance (AVUM) and Aviation Intermediate Maintenance (AVIM) Manual for General Aircraft Maintenance, Electrical and Instrument Maintenance Procedures and Practices, Volume 4, TM 1-1500-204-23-4
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of the Army / LOGSA; hosted by Chinook Helicopter public technical-manual archive
sources.use: Best primary-source public mechanical layout for conventional ASI and VSI behavior; not a matched component overhaul manual and not usable for dimensional reconstruction.
locator: PDF p.62, printed p.4-13, Figure 4-11: sectional airspeed-indicator drawing labels static/pitot connections, diaphragm, restraining spring, hairspring, rocking shaft, sector, long lever, handstaff pinion and pointer. Adjacent text describes capsule motion converted to pointer movement by mechanical linkage.

PDF p.63, printed p.4-14, text: conventional VSI includes two air-enclosing chambers, with a pressure-sensitive diaphragm directly connected to static pressure and an airtight case connected through a thin-walled porcelain capillary; diaphragm motion drives the pointer. This is source text rather than inference.

PDF p.64, printed p.4-15, Figure 4-12: conventional VSI sectional layout with internal diaphragm/chamber, mechanical linkage and case/capillary path. It is a section/layout view, not an exploded parts drawing.
PDF p.63, printed p.4-14, Table 4-1 gives ASI test tolerance values for MS28045/MS28021/MS28046 at specified knots. Those are performance limits, not physical dimensions.

sources.title: Airspeed Indicator Information, WPR11FA316
sources.publisher: National Transportation Safety Board, Office of Aviation Safety, Western Pacific Region
sources.use: Primary evidence that a real conventional aircraft ASI has a separate diaphragm/case gasket and the shown teardown relationships; use alongside the Army layout drawing, not as a scale drawing.
locator: PDF p.2 documents actual functional/leak test and removal/replacement of a failed diaphragm/case gasket.
PDF p.3, Figure 1: actual unit exploded-view drawing with gasket identified; PDF pp.4-5 show actual leak test and removed gasket.
The report states a bezel leak check at 18,000 ft and documents that a new diaphragm/case gasket eliminated the observed leak.

sources.title: AC 65-15A, Airframe & Powerplant Mechanics - Airframe Handbook
sources.use: FAA cross-check for conventional mechanism terminology; not a physical reconstruction source.
locator: Flight-instrument section describes a metallic ASI diaphragm, link, rocking shaft, sector with hairspring and pinion/tapered pointer shaft.
Describes VSI diaphragm and connecting linkage inside sealed case. This is mechanism overview, not model-specific part evidence.

sources.title: Vertical Speed Indicator, U.S. Patent 2,285,521
sources.publisher: United States Patent Office; PDF hosted by Google Patents patent-images storage

locator: Patent text and illustrations support an insulated chamber, restricted capillary, differential-pressure-responsive diaphragm, pointer linkage, and temperature-compensation features.

sources.title: Altimeter, U.S. Patent 5,016,473
sources.publisher: United States Patent Office; PDF hosted by Google Patents patent-images storage
sources.use: Only source found here with an explicit overall altimeter diameter and internal aneroid movement value; useful as a separately labeled patented compact design, not for the Kollsman model.
locator: Patent text states a 2-inch example overall diameter and a four-aneroid-element mechanism. It states 2.5 mm deformation for each element over the stated pressure range and a 5 mm deformation for each opposing cap assembly. These dimensions apply only to this patent design.
